newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes firm, ANS sold for -$2.08.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes firm, ANS sold for -$2.08.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices rose Wednesday, lifted by broadly higher markets and a smaller discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, traders said.

BP Oil sold a full cargo of ANS to a small Northwest refiner for $2.08 under September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, the first spot sale since a deal was completed in mid-June for $2.16 under August WTI.
A major West Coast refiner offered 900,000 barrels of Canadon Seco (Argentina) crude to other West Coast companies, traders said, declining to name the price.
One or two refiners could buy the cargo, which could load in late August and arrive to the West Coast in mid-September.
Spot prices rose in line with broader market gains, including a 35 cents a barrel rise in September spot WTI.
Kern River and Wilmington grades rose after Texaco raised its posted prices on Wednesday by 50 cents.
